channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: American History TV
channel.desc: Airing weekends, "American History TV" offers programming about people and events that document the American story, geared toward history aficionados. Shows that air under the "American History TV" banner cover the history of the nation, from its founding in the 18th century through modern times. Topics covered include the Civil War, presidents and the exploration of historical sites.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Tours the Louisville Slugger Museum & Factory
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the Louisville Slugger Museum & Factory to learn the history and cultural impact of the iconic baseball bat and see where they are crafted in downtown Louisville, Kentucky.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Historian and Herbert Hoover biographer George Nash reflects on the life and legacy of America's 31st president (1929-33). His essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Documentary filmmaker Ken Burns and historian Geoff Ward reflect on the life and legacy of President Franklin Roosevelt (1933-45). Their essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: Lectures in History
channel.desc: The Founding Fathers have inspired many writers and politicians, but who inspired the Founding Fathers? Fannie Bialek looks at the people who inspired early American political thought.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: George Washington's Draft Copy of the U.S. Constitution -- 1787
channel.desc: C-SPAN views all seven pages of George Washington's 1787 annotated copy of a draft of the U.S. Constitution, on display together for the very first time at the National Archives in Washington, D.C.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Historian and author Nancy Beck Young reflects on the life and legacy of First Lady Lou Hoover (1929-33). Her essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned by the organization More Perfect to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: The Presidency
channel.desc: Historian Diana Carlin analyzes the life of Julia Grant using the first lady's memoirs. The Ulysses S. Grant Historic Site hosts this event.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Tours the Latter-Day Saints Church History Museum
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the Church History Museum of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Salt Lake City.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Finalists for the 2026 George Washington Prize discuss their books on the nation's founding era at an event held at George Washington's Mount Vernon in Virginia.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Curator Abeer Saha walks C-SPAN's American History TV through an exhibition of more than 30 iconic objects brought together to explore the ideals expressed in the Declaration of Independence at the Smithsonian Castle in Washington, D.C.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: The Hearing Room
channel.desc: Anthea Hartig, historian and director of the National Museum of American History, testifies before the House Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency (DOGE) regarding accusations of political activism and rewriting history.

channel.name: CSPAN 3 US
channel.title: Book TV
channel.desc: This long-running staple of the C-SPAN2 weekend schedule helps expand the channel's programming beyond politics. Most episodes of "Book TV" feature discussions with authors of nonfiction books, usually in the form of interviews, lectures or seminars. The series sometimes includes coverage of major book fairs and festivals. Some of the notable names who have appeared on the show include David Mamet and Tom Clancy.
